title: Mystery Humans Lived in a Chinese Cave for 100,000 Years—We Just Found Their Arm Bone!
summary: Have you ever heard of Denisovans? They were a group of ancient humans who lived in Asia and went extinct about 30,000 years ago. Scientists know they existed because of DNA, but they've found very few of their bones. That's why a new discovery in a cave in China is so exciting! In Bianfu Cave in Yunnan province, scientists found five human fossils, including a piece of an arm bone called a radius. This is the first Denisovan arm bone ever found! The cave was used by Denisovans for more than 100,000 years, from about 190,000 to 70,000 years ago. The fossils date to between 134,000 and 167,000 years ago. Inside the cave, they also found nearly 1,400 stone tools and more than 64,000 animal bones. That tells us the Denisovans hunted big animals like cows and deer, and they used the tools to cut meat and even crack open bones to eat the marrow inside. The arm bone has an interesting shape—it's a bit like a Neanderthal's at the elbow, but more like a modern human's overall. Scientists think this might have helped them do precise tasks with their hands. This discovery helps us understand these mysterious ancient humans better. As one scientist said, they hope to find more Denisovan bones in the future to learn even more. Isn't it amazing what we can learn from a few old bones?
why_it_matters: This discovery shows that history is still full of puzzles, and a single bone can change what scientists think about our ancient relatives.

background_read: Denisovans are named after Denisova Cave in Siberia, where scientists first found their DNA.
The new finds are from Bianfu Cave in Yunnan province in China, far outside Siberia.
Comparing bones with Neanderthals (another ancient human group) helps show what made Denisovans different.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists searching inside Bianfu Cave in Yunnan province, China, found fossils from ancient humans called Denisovans.
WHAT: The cave was used for more than 100,000 years, and scientists found the first Denisovan arm bone, stone tools, and animal bones.
WHERE: Bianfu Cave in Yunnan province, China.
WHY: Denisovan bones are very rare, so this find gives new clues about how these ancient humans lived and used their hands.

perspectives.description: They are excited because Denisovan bones are so rare, and an arm bone can show how these humans moved and worked.
They find it amazing that people used one cave for over 100,000 years — much longer than any modern country has existed.
They hope even more Denisovan bones will turn up so the 'mystery humans' become less mysterious.
